page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the custom ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture with Neoverse-V2 cores. The configuration provides 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) operating at 2.8 GHz, with 1 thread per core. Memory allocation stands at 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). For high-throughput temporary storage, the instance bundles a dedicated 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps, and no GPUs are provisioned.

Benchmark results reveal balanced mid-tier compute capabilities alongside select decompression advantages. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests delivered 1,706.99 and 6,814.04 respectively, positioning the machine in the middle 50% band. Geekbench testing returned a single-core score of 1,860.0 and a multi-core score of 5,899.0, with solid performance in software compilation (8,616.0) and image processing (5,537.0). In data decompression tests, single-threaded bzip3 reached 14.18 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. However, PassMark metrics highlighted relative weaknesses, particularly in the CPU encryption suite (750.26) and extended instructions (3,679.01), both landing in lower tiers due to the lack of x86-specific vector execution extensions like AVX or AVX-512.

Memory bandwidth shows strong caching efficiency with 462.36 GB/sec across small 16 KB blocks, dropping to 96.66 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 42.75 GB/sec for writes. Throughput metrics demonstrate steady execution across web serving (10.09 GB/sec) and Redis SET operations (9.24 million ops/sec). Because this instance lacks hardware accelerators, large-scale deep learning is constrained; small model (135M) LLM text generation achieved 69.76 tokens/sec, while a 7B parameter model ran at 6.48 tokens/sec.

The c8gd.xlarge provides strong resource efficiency for applications that maximize dedicated ARM cores alongside high-speed local disk storage. The combination of dedicated Neoverse-V2 cores and direct NVMe storage makes it well aligned for continuous integration and build pipelines, batch processing, static web serving, and distributed database nodes that leverage local ephemeral scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 4-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processor running at 2.8 GHz with 1 thread per core. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and includes a 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark assessments, the instance displays consistent mid-tier compute performance, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 5,899.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving an upper-tier 14.18 GB/sec. Due to its ARMv9 architecture, it lacks x86 AVX instructions, reflecting lower PassMark CPU encryption scores. With its fast local NVMe cache and dedicated physical cores, the instance suits software compilation, CI/CD runners, containerized microservices, and web serving workloads.
